unique_original_proof: Let the common apex A be the origin and a radial leg have length r. In the displayed construction the consecutive triangles are T_n=conv{0,r u(theta+100n),r u(theta+100(n+1))}; the equal shared radial leg and identical 100-degree apex give fixed r and shape, not a growing logarithmic spiral. A full coincidence must preserve the unique 100-degree apex and both radial endpoints. The unswapped case requires 100n=0 mod360, first n=18 since gcd(100,360)=20. The swapped case requires simultaneously 100n=100 and 100n=-100 mod360, impossible because200 is not0 mod360. Thus neither parallel outer bases at n=9 nor equal shapes at n=2 give full coverage. Number18 is unique; counting the initial object gives19 objects, not index19.
